lines.text: Can a 10 dollar bottle of Lucas fix a transmission that the shop wants 1500 dollars to rebuild?
This 220000 mile Honda slips from second to third which is exactly what the bottle promises to stop.
He cooks it at 300 degrees for 2 hours and Lucas loses just 0.62 grams while normal fluid loses 1.3.
Because Lucas is basically thick oil which a lab found is about 3 times thicker than motor oil.
beats: ai:thick golden oil slowly pouring off a metal spoon in a garage macro
ai:thin amber motor oil pouring fast from a bottle next to thick honey colored oil

lines.text: So on the friction tester Lucas does far better because thick oil protects the metal from wear.
But at 20 below the plain fluid races down the slide while Lucas doesn't move until 2 minutes after it finished.
And a cold transmission needs thin fluid that can reach every clutch on a frozen morning.
beats: ai:a silver sedan parked outside covered in frost on a snowy winter morning
ai:cutaway of an automatic transmission clutch pack wet with red fluid macro

lines.text: So he adds all 24 ounces and the second to third shift gets better but it still hesitates on a hill.
So it's no real fix and he gives it maybe 15000 more miles but for 10 dollars it's worth a try.
Would you pour this into your car?

facts_checked: Whisper transcript LMyfq8ZxZc8 + frames: 2000 Honda Accord 220,000+ miles 0:13-0:18; shop wanted rebuild, owner won't spend $1500 0:37-1:04; 2nd-3rd slip 1:45-2:06 (captions 'Not good' 2:09, 'Some slip with quick acceleration' 2:18); bottle claims stops slip/hesitation 6:14 (label 6:15-6:21); evaporative test 200 g, ~300F, 2 h 2:47-2:51 (thermal 3:03 shows 325F); Lucas -0.62 g vs ATF -1.3 g 3:30-3:47 (captions 3:36/3:42); lubricity tester Lucas far better than ATF 5:26-5:30 (pins 5:27-5:33); -20F cold flow, Lucas out of gate 2 min after ATF finished 3:59, 5:35-5:59 (caption '2 minutes later' 6:00); lab SUS viscosity 179.5 vs 5W30 ~60, little additive package 9:32-9:53 (sheet 9:45); added 24 oz 6:58; after: better 2nd-3rd shift on light acceleration but still delay on hill climb (captions 7:27, 7:51, 8:21); not fixed, maybe 15-20k mile lifespan, $10-12 worth trying 9:58-10:32. Thin fluid needed when cold = general ATF knowledge (illustrated by the cold-flow test).
safety: no repair advice beyond the source's opinion; product not claimed to fix broken parts (as the label says)
